findings.element: interaction-check.mjs:1231 and :1250 — the two new RegExp(...) calls inside the august-inside-a-july-reading and refusals-written-in-the-studio-vocabulary blocks
findings.problem: Both patterns are built from the source literal "\\\\b" — four backslashes in the file, verified with od -c on line 1231. At runtime that is the string backslash-backslash-b, so the compiled pattern matches a LITERAL backslash followed by the letter b. I evaluated the file's own expression: re.source comes back as \\bAugust\\b(?!\\s+\\d{4}), and testing it against "in August it happened" returns false; the voice pattern for "callers" tested against "the callers are here" returns false. dates and voice.hits are therefore always empty arrays, and eight assertions — "no month is named without its year" and "the refusals speak the reader's language", each across full/partial/quiet/first-run — cannot fail. I ran the gate: 461 assertions, 0 failing, all eight reported pass. This is L-12 in the paid-for defect library ("Regexes written through a shell lose their escapes ... twice in gate assertions, where it silently made checks vacuous") creeping back inside the same engagement, in the doubling direction rather than the stripping one, and L-12's own remedy — verify a pattern against its own inputs before it lands — was not applied.
findings.consequence: Two of the honesty classes the panel already paid to find and fix have no guard at all, while the gate's assertion count reports that they do. Unanchored dates and studio vocabulary can both walk back onto the surface with the gate green — the exact mechanism L-05 records for seam-pick-desync, which was counted closed for three rounds. On a frozen surface the gate is the only thing left holding the work; eight of the 461 assertions it claims are decoration.
findings.fix: Rewrite both patterns with String.raw so the escapes cannot be doubled. Line 1231 becomes: const re = new RegExp(String.raw`\b${m}\b(?!\s+\d{4})`, "g"); line 1250 becomes: new RegExp(String.raw`\b${w}\b`, "i").test(text). With the escaping corrected the month check then fails on "May" in full, partial and quiet, because the week ruler prints "18 May" — I drove that and confirmed it. Scope the month check to prose so the ruler's day-and-month stamps are not read as bare month names: inside the evaluate, const main = document.querySelector("main") || document.body; const c = main.cloneNode(true); c.querySelectorAll(".chart").forEach(e => e.remove()); document.body.appendChild(c); const text = c.innerText; c.remove(); and run the corrected month regex over that. Driven across all seven states, the corrected month check over that prose returns [] and the corrected voice check over full main innerText returns [] — so the fix passes today's surface and can fail tomorrow's.
findings.assertion: Before either family runs, the gate proves its own patterns against a positive and a negative control and fails if they are inert: new RegExp(String.raw`\b${"August"}\b(?!\s+\d{4})`).test("in August it happened") === true, the same pattern .test("arrive on 10 August 2026") === false, and new RegExp(String.raw`\b${"callers"}\b`, "i").test("the callers are here") === true. A pattern that cannot match its own positive control is a dead rule and the gate says so out loud.

findings.problem: Round 2 made the document the scroller. .scroll now carries only overflow-x: clip (lately.html:180) and, by design, its overflow-y stays visible — so it is not a scroll container and scrollBy on it is a no-op. Driven at 390x844 with touch: getComputedStyle(.scroll) reads overflowX "clip", overflowY "visible", and scrollHeight === clientHeight === 2664. I pinned a tip with a real tap, then ran the gate's exact line: document.scrollingElement.scrollTop stayed at 1170 and .scroll.scrollTop stayed at 0. The assertion "a pinned label is dismissed or follows its mark" therefore judges a page that never moved, and after.drift is only the tip's resting 8px offset. It cannot fail for the r1 finding it exists to hold. The behaviour itself is sound — I then scrolled the document 260px for real and the tip stayed on and tracked its mark at drift 8 — so this is a dead guard sitting over a working fix. The same stale model is written into the source: the comment at lately.html:1147 still reads "The surface scrolls inside .scroll, not the document, so no scroll event reaches a window listener without capture", which has been false since round 2 and contradicts the CSS comment at lately.html:113 that says the document is the scroller.
findings.consequence: The one assertion protecting the tooltip's anchor under scroll — on the width where the tooltip is the only place a job's title lives — proves nothing. If a future change re-broke the anchor the gate would stay green. It also leaves a false mechanism recorded in the source, so the next person to touch the tip handler reasons from a scroller that no longer exists.
findings.fix: In interaction-check.mjs replace the scroll with document.scrollingElement.scrollBy(0, 260), and record document.scrollingElement.scrollTop before and after so the assertion fails if the surface did not actually move. In lately.html:1147 correct the comment to say the document is the scroller and that the capture-phase listener is kept because a scroll may still originate inside a nested scroller.
findings.assertion: "a pinned label is dismissed or follows its mark" first records document.scrollingElement.scrollTop before and after its own scroll and fails if the delta is under 200px; only on a page that demonstrably moved is the tip claim (dismissed, or drift <= 24px from its mark) evaluated.

findings.element: interaction-check.mjs:534 — ok("the previous best draws last, after the columns have grown", Number(early.record) < Number(late.record) || early.lastBar < late.lastBar)
findings.problem: The right-hand disjunct is the same condition line 532 uses to prove the entrance runs at all, and it is independently true for any entrance whose columns animate. Driven at ?motion=play with the gate's own sampling times, early.lastBar is 0 and late.lastBar is 168, so early.lastBar < late.lastBar is true on its own. If .record's 1.1s animation-delay were removed and the previous best drew simultaneously with the first column, the left disjunct would go false and the assertion would still pass. The ordering the assertion names — the old ceiling drawn last, after the reader has read the shape — is never tested by it.
findings.consequence: The choreography's one substantive claim, that the reader meets the shape before being told where the old ceiling was, has no guard. It is the only part of the entrance that carries an argument rather than a flourish, and it is the part the gate does not measure.
findings.fix: Drop the disjunct and test the order directly. At ?motion=play, poll the twelfth column's height until it stops changing (its animation-delay is 11*40+340 = 780ms over a 500ms duration, so it settles near 1300ms), sample getComputedStyle('.record').opacity at that frame and require it to be under 0.5, then sample again at 2000ms and require it to be 1.
findings.assertion: At motion=play, the previous best is still undrawn — computed opacity below 0.5 — at the frame the twelfth column first reaches its full height, and is fully drawn (opacity 1) by 2000ms. The check must be watched failing with .record's animation-delay set to 0 before it lands.

findings.element: lately.html:401 — .dot:hover, .dot:focus-visible { --disc: var(--ink); } — against the touch pin in the pointerdown handler at lately.html:1187
findings.problem: Under a coarse pointer the browser latches :hover onto the last element touched and never releases it. Driven at 390x844 with hasTouch and isMobile, using a real touchscreen.tap on the first mark: at rest the dot computes --disc #71717a; after one tap el.matches(':hover') is true and --disc is #111111 with the ::before ring at rgb(17, 17, 17); after the second tap that dismisses the tip (tip.classList.contains('on') === false) the mark is still #111111; after scrolling the document 300px it is still #111111. The mark is left carrying the surface's strongest ink with no state behind it — not pinned, not focused, not past the fortnight.
findings.consequence: The strip's entire reading is carried by fill and ink density: a hollow ring inside the fortnight, a solid indigo mark past it. A residue of an interaction the reader already dismissed makes one arbitrary young mark the most emphatic mark in the strip, and it stays that way for the rest of the session. 390 is the width where the tooltip is the only place a job's title lives, so it is the width where a reader taps marks most — every tap leaves another false emphasis behind. The lock's rule is that status is ink density and fill; this puts ink density on a mark that has no status.
findings.fix: Gate the hover branch on a fine pointer and give the pin its own mark. Replace .dot:hover, .dot:focus-visible { --disc: var(--ink); } with .dot:focus-visible { --disc: var(--ink); } then @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) { .dot:hover { --disc: var(--ink); } } then .dot.pinned { --disc: var(--ink); }, all still declared before .dot:active so the press keeps winning at equal specificity. In the script add el.classList.add("pinned") inside show(el, pin) when pin is true, and clear it in drop() with for (const d of root.querySelectorAll(".dot.pinned")) d.classList.remove("pinned"). No new colour, no new weight, no new object.
findings.assertion: At 390x844 with touch: after tapping a .dot and tapping it again to dismiss, every .dot computes --disc to its resting value (#71717a, or #4f46e5 for .old) and no dot's ::before box-shadow colour is rgb(17, 17, 17); and while one mark is pinned, exactly one .dot computes --disc to #111111 and it is the pinned one.

findings.element:
lately.html:645 —
, hidden by opacity: 0 at lately.html:410
findings.problem: The tip is hidden with opacity, not visibility, and its innerHTML is never cleared. Driven at 1440x960: focus the fourth mark, then blur it. #tip.innerHTML remains 6 days openApprove the final seating plan, computed opacity 0, visibility visible, aria-hidden null. A CDP Accessibility.getFullAXTree taken in that state carries two un-ignored StaticText nodes — "6 days open" and "Approve the final seating plan" — with empty ignoredReasons. role="presentation" removes the div's own role and leaves its text exposed. The element is a sibling of #root, so that text sits after the provenance footer, outside header, main and footer alike. The surface states the rule it is breaking, at lately.html:298: "visibility, not opacity: an opacity-0 label is invisible to the eye and fully present in the accessibility tree" — applied to .xaxis span.mute and not to the tip. Nothing guards it: the gate's "no invisible label carries live text" is scoped to .chart at interaction-check.mjs:1089 and the tip lives outside the whole app tree. It is also the surface's only element, which maps to a deletion role, used to carry a job title.
findings.consequence: A screen-reader reader who has tabbed the strip and then reads on reaches the end of the document and hears an unlabelled fragment — a day count and a job title — belonging to whichever mark they last visited, sitting outside every landmark with nothing to explain it. It is stale by construction: it survives blur, scroll and dismissal, so it names a mark the reader is no longer on. On an instrument whose whole argument is that you can always tell what it read and when, an orphaned reading is the wrong last thing to say.
findings.fix:
Add aria-hidden="true" to the tip element at lately.html:645, so it reads
. Every fact the tip carries is already on the dot's own aria-label (", open N days"), which is the accessible channel, and the tip is already pointer-events: none, so nothing else is lost.
findings.assertion: For every state, after focusing a .dot and then blurring it, #tip carries aria-hidden="true", and a full CDP accessibility tree contains no un-ignored node whose name matches #tip.textContent.

biggestWin: Repair the gate, because on a frozen surface the gate is the only thing left that keeps this finished. Ten of its 461 assertions cannot fail for the defect they name: eight because both string-built regexes carry doubled escapes and match a literal backslash (L-12, already paid for once in this engagement), one because it scrolls a container round 2 removed, one because a redundant disjunct makes its own claim untestable. Two of those families guard exactly the honesty classes this product's argument rests on — dates anchored to the stated reading, and refusals written in the owner's language rather than the studio's. The visible surface is essentially done. What stands between it and finished is roughly an hour, all of it polish and instrumentation, none of it a build and none of it a different decision: the five fixes above, plus the chart's 1.48:1 context columns, which are correctly on the port packet and for which I have no fix that does not invert the reading.
